claims: README.md says the 211-square packing combines a 64-square rectangular component from Arslanov, Mustafin and Shangitbayev (2021), a computationally found 30-square component, and two aligned grids containing 99 and 18 squares; that the numerical search and refinement were performed with GPT-6 Astra under the direction of Joost de Winter; and that earlier solutions and optimization scripts supplied to the model had been developed with Claude Opus and previous GPT models.

Its Sources section names M. Z. Arslanov, S. A. Mustafin and Z. K. Shangitbayev (2021), 'Improved packings of n(n - 1) unit squares in a square', The Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 28(4), P4.22, doi:10.37236/8586, as the source of the construction with tilted components combined with grids and of the 64-square rectangular component; Erich Friedman's collection of square packings (Packing Center, 'Squares in Squares') and his survey, E. Friedman (2009), 'Packing unit squares in squares: A survey and new results', The Electronic Journal of Combinatorics, Dynamic Survey DS7, doi:10.37236/28, as the source of the known packings used as starting points and for comparison; and David Ellsworth's records of square packings, used as starting points and for comparison.

Its Files section lists n211__record.json, the coordinates of the packing, and n211__record.svg, its figure: the same files, byte for byte, as at 702df9bb, which T-057 registers at side 14.99796070496771500150.
